k1983:
A 1+1 apartment in a residential complex under construction at Golem, three hundred and fifty metres from the sea.

The internal area is 43.87 m² with 11.89 m² of shared space: a living room, a bedroom and a bathroom, on the ground floor.

Buying at this stage is the trade at the centre of it. The price per square metre is lower than a finished flat nearby would cost, and the payment is spread across the build in four steps rather than falling due at once. What is given up in exchange is certainty about when it will be ready.

On that point: the completion date announced at the launch of this project has already passed. Ask for the revised date in writing, and read the penalty terms in the contract for a delay.
k1984: 63 m² 1+1 on the ground floor, new build at Golem
k1985: The largest ground-floor one-bedroom unit in this Golem block: 49.89 m² internal plus 13.52 m² shared, 350 m from the sea.
k1986:
A 1+1 apartment on the ground floor of a modern building under construction at Golem, three hundred and fifty metres from the shore.

The internal area is 49.89 m², with a further 13.52 m² of shared space: a living room, a bedroom and a bathroom. This is the most generous of the one-bedroom units on this level, and at close to fifty square metres inside it lives considerably better than the smaller ones.

The building stands on a main road with straightforward access, and the development is residential throughout.

Payment runs in four instalments alongside the construction. The completion date first given for the project has already passed, so ask the seller to put the current one in writing before signing.
k1987: 67 m² 1+1 in a new seaside block, Golem
k1988: A spacious one-bedroom unit of 52.88 m² internal plus 14.33 m² shared, on the ground floor, 350 m from the sea.
k1989:
A 1+1 apartment in a modern residential complex under construction at Golem, three hundred and fifty metres from the shore.

The internal area is 52.88 m², with 14.33 m² of shared space, on the ground floor: a living room, a bedroom and a bathroom. At nearly fifty-three square metres inside, this is among the larger one-bedroom layouts in the building — enough for a proper separation between the living area and the bedroom rather than a nominal one.

The block sits on a main road, is residential throughout, and payment is staged across the build: 40% on contract, 30% at shell completion, 20% when plastering begins and the last 10% on handover of the keys.

Before committing, note that the completion date originally published for this project has already passed. Ask the seller for the current date in writing and check what the contract says about delay.
k1990: 51 m² 1+1 in a new block 350 m from the sea, Golem
k1991: A compact one-bedroom unit: 40.38 m² internal plus 10.94 m² shared, ground floor, bought at the earliest stage of the build.
k1992:
A 1+1 apartment in a new residential complex at Golem, three hundred and fifty metres from the sea.

The internal area is 40.38 m², plus 10.94 m² of shared space, on the ground floor: a living room, a bedroom and a bathroom. It is a small flat and reads as one — the appeal is the location and the entry price rather than the space.

As a rental proposition near the coast this size works well: a one-bedroom is the format holidaymakers look for, and the running costs of a forty-square-metre flat are modest.

Payment is in four instalments following the construction. Construction is at its early stage, and the completion date first announced has already passed — the current one should be confirmed in writing before anything is signed.
k1993: Studio of 48 m² in a new complex 350 m from the sea, Golem
k1994: Studios from 37.22 m² internal plus 10.87 m² shared, ground floor, in a Golem block under construction.
k1995:
Studios in a new residential complex under construction at Golem, three hundred and fifty metres from the shore.

The internal area starts at 37.22 m², with 10.87 m² of shared space, on the ground floor: one room and a bathroom. Several are on offer and the figure quoted is the starting size, so ask for the schedule of the actual units and their areas — they are not all the same.

A studio this close to the beach is bought for letting more often than for living: it is the cheapest way into the complex, and the seasonal rental market on this stretch of coast takes small units readily.

Payment is staged with the build in four instalments. Work is at an early stage and the completion date announced at launch has already passed — get the current one in writing.
k1996: 71 m² 2+1 in a new block near the sea, Golem
k1997: A two-bedroom unit of 55.93 m² internal plus 11.16 m² shared, on the ground floor, 350 m from the shore.
k1998:
A 2+1 apartment in a modern block under construction at Golem, three hundred and fifty metres from the shore.

The internal area is 55.93 m², with 11.16 m² of shared space, on the ground floor: a living room, two bedrooms and one bathroom. Two bedrooms inside fifty-six square metres means compact rooms — worth seeing the plan before deciding, since the second bedroom in layouts of this size is usually a single.

One bathroom serving two bedrooms is the other thing to weigh if the flat is meant for a family or for letting to two couples.

The complex is residential throughout and sits on a main road. Payment runs in four instalments across the build. The completion date announced when the project launched has passed, so ask for the current one in writing.
k1999: Furnished 2+1 in Lura 1, 70 m from the sea, Gjiri i Lalzit
k2000: A furnished two-bedroom apartment with a balcony on the third floor of the Lura 1 resort complex, seventy metres from the beach.
k2001:
A 2+1 apartment in the Lura 1 complex at Gjiri i Lalzit, one of the most sought-after stretches of the Albanian coast.

The gross area is 70 m² and the net 54 m², on the third floor: a living room with kitchen, two bedrooms, one bathroom and a balcony. It is sold furnished, which means it can be let or lived in from the day the keys change hands — no fit-out year, no furniture budget.

The beach is seventy metres away. That distance is the whole point of Gjiri i Lalzit and it is why prices here sit well above the Durrës average: the bay is a planned resort area rather than ordinary coastal town, and the season runs strongly.

At this price the figure per square metre is high for Albania. It buys the address and the rental demand that comes with it, and that trade is worth making consciously rather than by accident.
k2002: Two studios sold together, 146 m² with a large veranda, Plazh Hekurudha
k2003: Two studios on the sixth floor near Hotel Antalya: 73 m² of interior and 73 m² of veranda. No lift in the building.
k2004:
Two studios at Plazh Hekurudha in Durrës, near Hotel Antalya, sold as one lot.

The gross area is 146 m², of which 73 m² is interior and 73 m² veranda — two separate units, each with its own bathroom, on the sixth floor. The veranda is as large as the living space, which on this side of Durrës means outdoor room that is usable for most of the year.

Two things to be clear about. First, this is one purchase of two flats, not a single 146 m² apartment: they can be let separately, which is the sense of the arrangement, but they are not one home. Second, the building has no lift and these are on the sixth floor — that matters every day for anyone living here, and it matters for guests carrying luggage if the units are let out.

The price reflects both the walk-up and the seaside position. For letting, the layout is efficient: two independent lets from one deal, on a beach that fills every season.
k2005: Furnished 3+1 of 150 m², 100 m from the sea, Shkëmbi i Kavajës
k2006: A large three-bedroom apartment on the fifth floor with a lift, sold furnished, a hundred metres from the shore.
k2007:
A 3+1 apartment at Shkëmbi i Kavajës, one of the most sought-after parts of the Durrës coastline, a hundred metres from the sea.

The gross area is 150 m² and the net 142.5 m² — an unusually small gap between the two, meaning most of what is paid for is floor you can stand on. The layout is a living room with kitchen, three bedrooms, one bathroom and a balcony, on the fifth floor, with a lift in the building. It is sold furnished, and the ownership documents are in order.

One point to weigh before viewing: three bedrooms served by a single bathroom. For a family using the flat full-time that is the thing most likely to grate, and with 142 m² of net floor there may be room to add a second — worth asking whether the plumbing allows it.

Otherwise this is a generous, quiet, ready-to-use flat within a short walk of the beach, at a price per square metre that is reasonable for the address.
k2008: Two-storey house on a 700 m² plot, renovated in 2022, Shkozet
k2009: A private house at Shkozet with 320 m² of built area over two floors, a walled garden, and a garage and store on the ground floor.
k2010:
A private two-storey house at Shkozet in Durrës, seven hundred metres from the overpass.

The plot is 700 m². The ground floor is 140 m² and holds a garage and a storeroom; the upper floor is 180 m² and is the living accommodation — a living room with a separate kitchen, three bedrooms and a bathroom. The house was renovated in 2022, is roofed and walled, and the garden and yard are private.

The ground floor is the interesting part. As it stands it is utility space, but it is 140 m² of it, at street level, behind its own wall — it converts to a second dwelling, a workshop or a business premises without touching the family's floor above. That optionality is most of what distinguishes this house from a flat of similar money.

What one bathroom for three bedrooms means in daily use is worth thinking through, and with a ground floor this size the room to add a second is there.

Shkozet is a settled residential quarter with everything to hand, close to the Durrës–Tirana road.
k2011: Furnished 2+1 of 90 m² on the sixth floor, Plazh Hekurudha
k2012: A well-furnished two-bedroom flat with a balcony, in a building with a lift, in the quiet part of Plazh Hekurudha.
k2013:
A 2+1 apartment at Plazh Hekurudha in Durrës.

The gross area is 90 m² and the net 82.4 m² — again a small gap, so the flat lives close to its headline size. Inside: a living room with kitchen, two bedrooms, one bathroom and a balcony, on the sixth floor, with a lift. The furnishing is described as good quality, the cubic measurement is registered correctly and the mortgage documentation is in order.

The quarter is residential and quiet, a short distance from the beach, and the sixth floor with a lift gives the thing a top-floor flat in Durrës is bought for: light, air and a view over the roofs rather than into the neighbour's window.

Worth checking on the viewing: which way the balcony faces and what is built in front of the building, since at this height that is what decides whether the sea is visible or merely nearby.
k2014: 1+1 of 64 m² in Liburna Residence, Golem
k2015: A west-facing third-floor flat, 53.3 m² net, in a Golem residence whose construction is nearly finished.
k2016:
A 1+1 apartment in Liburna Residence at Golem, in a quiet and well-regarded pocket of the area.

The gross area is 64 m², net 53.3 m², with 10.7 m² of shared space: a living room with kitchen, a bedroom, a bathroom and a balcony, on the third floor, in a building with a lift. The flat faces west.

West-facing matters more here than the word usually suggests. On this coast it means the afternoon and the sunset come into the rooms, which is what people buy a holiday flat for — and it also means the west side is the hot side in July, so shading the balcony is the first thing most owners do.

The building is in its final stage of construction rather than on paper: much of the risk that goes with an off-plan purchase has already been worked through, and the wait is short. Ask for the handover date in writing all the same.

At this price the flat sits in the range where a Golem one-bedroom is bought either as a holiday base or to let through the season, and it works for both.
k2017: 1+1 of 73 m² near the hospital, Durrës — top floor, no lift
